name: Merge Sort
description: Divide-and-conquer algorithm that splits the array in half, recursively sorts each half, then merges the sorted halves. Guarantees O(n log n) in all cases.
aim: Sort by recursively splitting until single elements, then merge pairs of sorted sub-arrays, combining the sorted order at each level until the full array is sorted.
howItWorks: Split array at midpoint into left and right halves
Merge: compare front elements of both halves, take the smaller
Continue merging until one sub-array is exhausted, append remainder

time.bestCase: Always divides evenly — log n levels × n merge work
time.averageCase: Divide-and-conquer guarantees log n depth always
time.worstCase: Worst case never degrades — guaranteed performance

realWorld: Java Arrays.sort for objects — guaranteed stability matters
Sorting linked lists — merge is natural for linked structure
External sort — merge sorted chunks from disk
Parallel processing — halves can be sorted simultaneously
whenToUse: Stable O(n log n) sort required
External merge sort for large datasets
alternatives: Quick Sort — better cache performance, in-place, but unstable
Heap Sort — in-place O(n log n) but not stable
Tim Sort — optimized hybrid used in production (Java, Python)
